People of Ukl or Uraina, healed by camels' milk and urine, killed the herdsman and drove off the camels; their hands and feet were cut, eyes branded, water withheld.
Uraina men given the Zakat camels' milk and urine killed the shepherd and drove off the camels; caught, they had hands and feet cut and eyes branded.
The Prophet sends Unais to stone a man's wife if she confesses illegal sexual intercourse, and has those present beat a drunk man with shoes and palm-leaf stalks.
A woman's hand was cut off for theft at the Conquest, after which she repented and married, and an unmarried adulterer was ordered a hundred lashes and a year's exile.
Sending an expedition, the Prophet first orders two named men of Quraish burnt, then withdraws it at the farewell: only Allah punishes with fire, so kill them if captured.
Withdrawing an order to burn two men, the Prophet says only Allah punishes with fire; Ibn Abbas says he would have killed, not burnt, the people Ali burnt.
Abu Qilaba said killing is lawful only for a married adulterer, a murderer or one waging war on Allah and His Apostle, citing men who killed a shepherd.
Sick men sent to drink the Prophet's camels' milk and urine recovered, killed his shepherd and drove off the camels; caught, they had hands and feet cut and eyes branded.
Taking a pledge against polytheism, theft and illegal intercourse, the Prophet said a legal punishment for such a sin expiates it, while one Allah screens is left to His will.
Beyond Allah's set punishments none gets over ten stripes; the Prophet prolonged a fast as if punishing wisal-fasters, resellers of unmoved food were beaten, and he avenged only for Allah.
